title: Embedded job queue; asynchronous crawl, map and batch scrape over MCP and loopback REST (Windows)

dependency_notes.SG-000108: Closed. crawl.rs, crawl_scope.rs, map_rank.rs, robots and sitemaps (slice 7, #317) are reused in place with their limits: at most 50 pages, depth 5, 10 minutes and 1,000 remembered URLs.

packets: WP1-06 (jobs, WebCrawlRequest to CrawlSpec translation, FetchCrawlDriver)
objective: Add crates/orcel-jobs, an embedded durable job queue with no server database and no async runtime (per-unit leases, per-origin politeness throttle callable by crawl drivers, bounded retry for read-only batch units, batch concurrency 1 to 4, a progress log used for reporting, a result store capped per job and globally with expiry, job ownership per principal). One crawl or map job is one unit: crawl.rs keeps the frontier, dedup, scope and limits through its CrawlDriver trait; per-URL units and dedup apply to batch scrape only. Add FetchCrawlDriver (fetch engine on the Windows SG-000040 transport) beside the existing WorkerCrawl (chromium). Expose them through Firecrawl v2 routes (POST /v2/map, POST /v2/crawl, GET and DELETE /v2/crawl/{id}, GET /v2/crawl/{id}/errors, /v2/crawl/ongoing and /active, POST /v2/batch/scrape and its status, cancel and errors routes, with v1 aliases for map and crawl) and the MCP tools web_map, web_crawl_start, web_batch_scrape_start, web_job_status, web_job_cancel, web_job_errors and web_job_list.

include: crates/orcel-jobs: queue, throttle, retry, concurrency, checkpoint and store modules (section 4.11 of the spec); the job state machine of section 4.7 with no new state; restart handling (not_started to cancelled, dispatched to outcome_unknown).

orceld: capabilities web/map, web/crawl_start, web/batch_scrape_start, job/status, job/cancel, job/errors, job/list; WebCrawlRequest to CrawlSpec translation in crates/orceld/src/web_dispatch.rs; FetchCrawlDriver in crates/orceld/src/fetch_crawl.rs; one SOFT approval per job bound to the canonical spec digest, the start origin's resolved-address set, engine, limits, principal and orcel_session_id (subject to FD-UP-5); TARGET_STALE on address drift; cancel, lease-independent emergency stop and approval-prompt expiry reach the job.
orcel-web: map, crawl and batch request types and the status mapping of section 5.5.
apps/orcel-mcp: the seven tool_contract entries (local_only) and the loopback routes listed in the objective, with job ownership and per-principal bounds.
tests/firecrawl-compat rows for map, crawl and batch, and the J-2 cancel probe.
exclude: Webhooks or any outbound callback from a job.
Subdomains, external links or whole-domain crawls (one admitted destination).
Crawl prompts, extract and other model-backed rows (Wave 3).
Any web job on macOS or Linux (WP2-12, SG-000115).
Any Firecrawl AGPL file; any Crawlee or Scrapling file copied verbatim.

authority_delta.jobs: Proposed: bounded asynchronous web jobs (per crawl at most 50 pages, depth 5, 10 minutes; at most 50 URLs per batch; 8 queued and 2 running device-wide; 4 queued and 1 pending approval per principal; 20 MiB per job and 200 MiB across jobs, expiring after 24 h) admitted by one SOFT approval per job spec in Safe mode. This is an explicit loosening of SG-000040's one-shot fetch approval for these shapes only and needs FD-UP-5. No new network class, no listener beyond the existing loopback server, no persistent browser profile, no job egress.

decisions.question: Job approval granularity in Safe mode (explicit loosening of SG-000040 one-shot fetch approval and C-04)
Crawl bounds
decisions.status: PENDING (FD-UP-11); this draft keeps SG-000108 slice 7's limits

invariants: Job states are exactly not_started, dispatched, completed, cancelled and outcome_unknown.
outcome_unknown is never retried automatically; mutating units are never retried.
A job approval binds the canonical spec digest, the resolved-address set and orcel_session_id, and cannot be replayed for a different spec, address set or session.
On restart no job resumes: not_started jobs are cancelled and dispatched jobs end as outcome_unknown.
crawl.rs alone owns the crawl frontier, dedup, scope and limits.
The crawl origin is the boundary; filters only narrow it.
Only the owning principal can read or cancel a job.
Result storage is bounded per job and globally, expires, and lives under the private state root.
acceptance: State machine property tests show no transition outside the table of section 4.7, including restart.
Crash test passes on all three OSes (orcel-jobs is platform-independent).
Per-origin delay is honoured within 10 ms of the configured value.
The J-2 cancel probe passes on Windows: cancelled within 2 s of the acknowledgement, and no fixture request after it beyond the in-flight page.
A change in the start origin's resolved-address set stops the job with TARGET_STALE.
Every W1 map, crawl and batch row of the parity matrix passes the SDK harness on Windows.
A fresh-context security judge passes the orceld dispatch slice.
